netbios_nbstat_disclosure.title: NetBIOS NBSTAT Information Disclosure (UDP/137)
netbios_nbstat_disclosure.description: The host responds to NBSTAT (NetBIOS name service status) queries on UDP/137 and discloses its NetBIOS machine name and MAC address without authentication.
netbios_nbstat_disclosure.impact: Reveals the host's NetBIOS computer name (often the AD computer-account name) and MAC address. Attackers use the MAC for OUI-based vendor fingerprinting and the NetBIOS name for AD reconnaissance. Combined with port 445/SMB, this is a building block for null-session enumeration.
netbios_nbstat_disclosure.remediation: Disable NetBIOS over TCP/IP on the network adapter if SMB-direct (port 445) is being used instead. On Windows: NIC properties → IPv4 → Advanced → WINS tab → "Disable NetBIOS over TCP/IP". On servers, ensure NetBIOS is bound only to management interfaces.
netbios_nbstat_disclosure.evidence_template: nbtscan against {{host}}:137 returned NetBIOS name "{{netbios_name}}" with MAC {{mac}}

netbios_server_role.title: NetBIOS Server Role Detected
netbios_server_role.description: NBSTAT response includes the <server> role indicator, meaning the host advertises itself as a NetBIOS file/print server.
netbios_server_role.impact: Informational — confirms the host has SMB-share-related services running. Cross-reference with port 445 findings (SMB null session, unsigned SMB, etc.) for compound severity.
netbios_server_role.remediation: If this host is not intended to provide file or print sharing, disable Server service. If it IS intended, ensure shares require authentication and SMB signing is mandatory.
netbios_server_role.evidence_template: Host {{host}} (NetBIOS name {{netbios_name}}) advertises <server> role on UDP/137
